PullRequest.Title: eslint: fix bracket notation in app environment
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- replace bracket notation with dot notation for identifier-like properties in the Application bootstrap, server, and environment cleanup group
- remove all 41 cleaned paths in that group from `.eslint-allowed-bracket-notation-files`

This PR is intentionally stacked on #334756, which enables `local/code-no-bracket-notation-for-identifiers`. Its base should be changed to `main` after #334756 merges.

## Validation

- targeted ESLint with `--max-warnings=0` across all 41 cleaned files
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run transpile-client`
- focused unit tests for `bootstrapESM.test.ts`, `environmentMainService.test.ts`, and `userDataPath.test.ts` — 10 tests passed
- targeted hygiene across all 42 changed files
- `git diff --check`

Scenarios.Scenario: Desktop application bootstrap and workbench startup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Command-line/environment checks select sandboxing, portability, NLS, code-cache, ASAR, and development behavior; startup then awaits bootstrapESM and the Electron main bundle before the application can progress. Every changed operation on this path is an equivalent identifier property access replacing bracket notation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load product/package metadata, inspect portable paths, and resolve/load startup modules.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A bounded set of startup reads/checks once per process; no added iteration or duplicate lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same branches and filesystem/module operations were selected using bracket property access.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing operations are on cold startup; the changed property syntax neither adds calls nor moves them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize the existing main-process/window communication path after bootstrap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing startup initialization and one send per open-files action; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same argument and environment values reached the same IPC paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: IPC remains downstream of bootstrap and is not newly awaited or multiplied.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One application process plus the existing number of windows/open-file actions; no changed collection cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Bootstrap and module loading remain serialized by existing awaits; window/process startup concurrency is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Code-cache, ASAR, and memoized environment decisions use the same keys and conditions; cold and warm behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that no expensive work, retained state, or scheduling changed; all relevant hunks only replace equivalent property syntax.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material: dot and bracket access are equivalent for all converted identifier-like keys.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: startup boundary count, ordering, and cache selection are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Local and remote CLI invocation, including tunnel, window launch, stdin, and IPC commands
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Argument parsing selects either a tunnel/CLI child process, a desktop process spawn, stdin file handling, or one IPC request; those existing operations remain the command's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn the tunnel binary, CLI process, Electron executable, macOS open command, or remote command process according to existing flags.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected subprocess per invocation, except existing profiling callbacks; unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical parsed flags selected identical spawn branches via bracket access.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The selected child remains the command execution path; no additional spawn or await was added.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send status, extension-management, or open requests to the existing CLI pipe.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC request per selected command; extension IDs remain grouped in one message.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request object and grouped inputs were sent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The response remains awaited for status/extension commands; no placement change.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read stdin into one temporary file, create a wait marker, or inspect a CLI version directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bounded per invocation, with stdin bytes scaling only with supplied input as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same flag values drove the same file operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing file work remains conditional on the same flags.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: CLI arguments, extension ID list, and stdin byte length; the diff does not alter effective cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most the existing selected child process or IPC request is launched for a command; process callbacks remain joined with Promise.all and no new fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache or cache-key change; lazy import of cliProcessMain remains limited to extension/telemetry operations.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from tracing each changed flag/environment read to unchanged spawn, IPC, and filesystem branches.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Platform-specific process duration varies, but the diff does not change whether or how often boundaries execute.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: command boundary fan-out and critical-path waits are identical.

Scenarios.Scenario: Remote server startup and web client/static-file requests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Server startup resolves host/port and loads the server module before listening; each HTTP request then reaches the existing handler, with static files performing stat and stream work and workbench HTML performing template reads.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probe/bind the configured port and handle HTTP/WebSocket traffic.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One listener startup plus one handler invocation per request/upgrade; unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Equivalent host, port, compatibility, and header values selected the same network operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Binding remains on startup and request handling remains per request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat and stream static files; read the workbench template and, only for the test resolver, two extension manifests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stat per static request, one stream on cache miss, one template read per workbench response, and two manifest reads only in test-resolver mode; unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same ETag and template values were assigned with bracket notation; no read was added or moved.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing reads remain on their respective response paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Incoming request count and response file size; test-resolver manifest count remains fixed at two.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The Node HTTP server continues handling requests with its existing event-loop concurrency; no new parallel requests, queues, or sequential loops are introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ETag requests still return 304 after the existing stat; no-expiry assets retain browser caching, and no cache key or invalidation changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence because the modified header/template assignments are semantically equivalent and do not alter I/O placement.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Request volume varies, but per-request work and cache behavior are demonstrably unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: network and filesystem work per request remains identical.

Scenarios.Scenario: Unix shell environment resolution and remote terminal variable lookup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On macOS/Linux when not skipped, shell environment resolution performs one shell discovery/spawn and parses its output before callers receive the environment; terminal variable getters then read resolved values locally.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn the user's login shell to serialize its environment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One spawn per process because unixShellEnvPromise caches both cold in-flight and warm results.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same environment keys were restored/deleted after parsing, and the same single cached spawn occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first eligible caller still awaits the shell; subsequent callers share the same promise.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of callers does not increase subprocess count due to existing promise coalescing; environment byte size is unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A module-level promise coalesces all shell-environment callers into one spawn; cancellation and timeout behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold path creates one promise/spawn; warm and concurrent calls reuse unixShellEnvPromise. Keys and lifecycle are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the explicit module-level promise and unchanged spawn path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Login-shell duration is user-dependent, but the diff cannot alter spawn cardinality or output size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: coalescing, subprocess count, and parsing work are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Diagnostics collection and remote extension installation/scanning
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Diagnostics reads and parses one launch.json before aggregating configurations; server extension setup batches requested builtin and user extensions, serializing user installation after builtin installation before readiness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse workspace .vscode/launch.json for diagnostics.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per requested workspace folder, followed by O(configurations) local aggregation; unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same configurations array and type values were traversed through bracket access.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The read remains required for that diagnostics request only.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve/download requested marketplace extensions through the existing extension-management batch API.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one grouped builtin install call and one grouped user install call; effective extension cardinality is the supplied deduplicated/processed list, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The force/category flags were read with bracket notation and passed to the same batched calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Server readiness still waits on the existing serialized install promises when install arguments are present.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Scan installed extensions and install local VSIX inputs through extension management.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Scales with supplied extension inputs as before; the diff does not add per-extension boundary calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same arguments reached the same extension management methods.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing install/scan work remains conditional on explicit CLI arguments.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of launch configurations and requested extension IDs; no loop, grouping, or deduplication behavior changed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Launch configuration aggregation remains a local loop after one read. Extension installs remain two grouped calls at most, intentionally sequenced by promises.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache key or lifecycle changes; readiness promises continue sharing install completion, and diagnostics remains uncached as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from direct before/after equivalence at the changed lines and unchanged grouped call sites.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Extension download/install time varies by extension and network, but invocation count and sequencing are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: no added I/O, fan-out, serialization, or repeated work.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 42 changed files and every diff page. The PR consistently replaces bracket notation with dot notation for identifier-like properties; traced startup, subprocess, IPC, filesystem, network, cache, batching, and lifecycle paths retain equivalent behavior. No actionable performance finding or regression-fix learning record is warranted.
